title: Stopping Wind and Water Erosion
seo_title: Grade 2 Erosion Worksheets: Compare Ways to Stop Wind and Water Changing the Land
standard_text: Compare multiple solutions designed to slow or prevent wind or water from changing the shape of the land.
meta_desc: Free grade 2 science worksheets on stopping erosion (NGSS 2-ESS2-1): plants, fences, walls and sandbags, model hill tests and comparing solutions. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Slow the wind. Slow the water.
key_sub: Plants, fences and walls help. Test them to find the best.
body_html:
How to think about it

We can slow down wind and water.

  • Plants and trees: roots hold soil, trees block wind.
  • Walls, fences, rocks and sandbags.
  • Test solutions and compare.
Example

Rain washes soil off a hill. What can help?

Roots hold soil.

Answer: plant grass

Example

Test: bare hill lost 9 spoons, rocks lost 3. Which works better?

Less sand lost is better.

Answer: rocks

Common mistakes

  • Picking the bigger number. Less sand lost is better.
  • Testing hills with different amounts of water.
  • Forgetting cost and time. Some solutions take years.

faq.a: Wind or water moving soil, sand or rock away, changing the shape of the land.
Plant grass and trees, build fences, walls and levees, put down rocks or sandbags.
Build small sand hills, cover each one differently, pour the same water on each and measure the sand that washes away.

items.q: What can slow down strong wind on a farm?
items.e: Trees block wind.

items.q: Ben reads: “Rain washes soil off a garden bed.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Ravi reads: “A river floods and washes away its banks.” What is changing the land here?
items.e: This change is caused by water.

items.q: Why do people put sandbags by doors in a flood?

items.q: Sam sees a problem: Waves wash away a sandy beach. What is a good solution?
c: use a fan to blow harder
put big rocks along the shore
items.e: Put big rocks along the shore: the rocks take the force of the waves.

items.q: How do plant roots help stop erosion?

items.e: Roots grip the soil.

items.e: Solutions slow wind or water.
